question: Does the Google Docs API requiredRevisionId protect the content of the existing run-owned native test Doc when a second update uses a stale revision?
kind: Pre-registered bounded live protocol probe; it does not enable native Cirrove writeback or establish document fidelity.
authorization_boundary: The owner authorized continued Google testing on run-owned objects. This probe may modify only the exact Doc created in the Cirrove Validation folder by google-native-import-live.json. It must not touch existing Workspace content or the installed Cirrove mounts.
prerequisite: The Google Docs API is currently disabled in the Cirrove Google Cloud project. Its project-level activation is a separate browser action and must be confirmed at action time before this live probe can start.
api_console_recheck: The docs.googleapis.com product page in the Cirrove Google Cloud project still displays 'Diese API aktivieren' and notes that using the product accepts Google APIs Terms of Service. No project setting was changed during this read-only recheck.
official_contract: https://developers.google.com/workspace/docs/api/reference/rest/v1/documents/batchUpdate documents that requiredRevisionId rejects a request when it is no longer the latest revision.
scope_preflight: The official documents.get reference accepts drive.readonly and the documents.batchUpdate reference accepts the full drive scope already requested by Cirrove's writable Google connections. This probe needs the Docs API enabled in the existing project, but no additional OAuth scope: https://developers.google.com/workspace/docs/api/reference/rest/v1/documents/get ; https://developers.google.com/workspace/docs/api/reference/rest/v1/documents/batchUpdate .
token_preflight: The private probe refuses to start unless its saved access token has at least 300 seconds remaining. The observed token would expire before the separate one-hour Shared Drive run ends; recheck the keyring after that run and allow Cirrove's broker to refresh it rather than sending a native write with an about-to-expire grant.
request_safety: The private probe accepts only exact HTTPS Docs and Drive API origins and refuses redirects before a bearer token can be forwarded elsewhere. It records HTTP statuses, hashes and booleans, never response bodies or opaque revision IDs.
arms: A: confirm the exact run-owned Drive item ID, Shared Drive ID, parent folder and native Doc MIME; read its Docs revision ID without logging the opaque revision
B: insert one small unique marker through documents.batchUpdate with the current requiredRevisionId, then require a newer Docs revision and exported text containing that marker
C: insert a distinct marker using the stale original requiredRevisionId; require a rejected request and repeated exact-ID exports retaining B but excluding C
endpoint: Pass only if B succeeds, C is rejected, and repeated exact-ID readback shows the rejected marker was never applied. Any uncertainty fails closed and leaves native writeback disabled.
prediction: The Docs-specific requiredRevisionId path should reject the stale update without changing content, unlike the observed Drive v2 native media upload. This is a hypothesis, not an implemented capability.
limits: One small plain-text edit on one owned Doc cannot establish DOCX import, formatting fidelity, multi-tab behavior, concurrent collaboration, Sheets safety or large exports.
